office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Republican incumbent Rob Chase faces first-time Democratic candidate Rob Tupper after a close primary (43% to 41%). The race turns on Chase's bill to create two autonomous regions within Washington, which Tupper opposes, and on taxes: Chase voted against the 2026 income tax and Tupper would keep it.

candidates.summary: Two-term State Representative and former Spokane County treasurer whose signature proposal would divide Washington into two autonomous regions.
highlights: Voted against the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and the 2025 B&O and services tax bills [S4][S6][S7]
Prime sponsor of HB 2085 to create autonomous Puget Sound and Columbia regions [S8]
Says human activity does not affect climate change and calls the Climate Commitment Act the most damaging tax [S9][S10]
Supported the parental-rights and girls'-sports initiatives and voted against ESHB 1296 [S5][S9]

taxes.basis: Voted no on ESSB 6346 and on the 2025 B&O (EHB 2081) and services excise (ESSB 5814) tax bills; pledges to lower taxes for everyone.

climate.basis: Says climate change is not human-caused, the state should not act to slow it, and the Climate Commitment Act is 'taxing the air'.

experience.basis: Two House terms and eight years as county treasurer, facing a first-time candidate.

local-control.basis: Sponsors HB 2085 to devolve state government to two autonomous regions with their own governors, judges and legislators.

social.basis: Opposes abortion except for ectopic pregnancy and supported the initiative barring athletes assigned male at birth from girls' sports; cites a perfect Family Policy Institute score.

parental-rights.basis: Supported the I-1 parental-rights initiative, voted against ESHB 1296 and for faster parent access to special-education evaluations.

tech.basis: Supports building AI data centers unless they significantly affect nearby residents.

candidates.summary: Retired teacher, engineer and commercial fisherman running as a Democrat for the first time, centering opposition to splitting the state, universal healthcare and keeping the income tax.
highlights: Would focus on maintaining the 2026 tax on income over $1 million [S6]
Pledges to fight for universal healthcare coverage [S3]
Lists "No Data Centers" as his first issue [S3]
Calls for community-oriented policing coordinated with social services [S1]

taxes.basis: Would focus on maintaining the tax on income over $1 million; website argues the sales-tax-reliant system is regressive.

healthcare.basis: Website pledges universal healthcare coverage; interested in partnering with Whole Washington, a universal-healthcare group.

tech.basis: Opposes data centers; 'No Data Centers' is his lead website issue, citing power, water, land and tax breaks.

safety.basis: Frames crime around root causes and backs police-clinician co-deployment and community-oriented policing coordinated with social services.

climate.basis: Says fossil-fuel use drives climate change; favors carbon-credit funds for building efficiency, forests and nuclear research.

experience.basis: First run for office; describes himself as 'not a career politician' against a two-term incumbent.

social.basis: Says government should not interfere in private matters like abortion; no stated position on LGBTQ+ issues.
